### Start development server inside an example directory

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Runs the development server for a specific example.

```bash
pnpm run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Run example applications

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/lit-query/README.md

Start the development servers for the basic, pagination, or SSR runnable Lit example projects from the repository root.

```bash
pnpm --dir examples/lit/basic run dev
pnpm --dir examples/lit/pagination run dev
pnpm --dir examples/lit/ssr run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Install dependencies and start Next.js development server

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/examples/react/nextjs-app-optimistic-updates/README.md

Installs project dependencies and runs the development server on localhost:3000.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Start development server with npm run dev

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/examples/svelte/load-more-infinite-scroll/README.md

Runs the local development server after installing dependencies. Use the `--open` flag to automatically launch the application in a new browser tab.

```bash
npm run dev

# or start the server and open the app in a new browser tab
npm run dev -- --open
```

### Invalidate queries by key prefix

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/query-invalidation.md

Invalidates matching queries starting with the specified queryKey prefix. In this example, both the base 'todos' and the parameterized 'todos' queries are invalidated.

```ts
import { injectQuery, QueryClient } from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'

class QueryInvalidationExample {
  readonly queryClient = inject(QueryClient)

  invalidateQueries() {
    this.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
  }

  // Both queries below will be invalidated
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos', { page: 1 }],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
}
```

--------------------------------

### useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin via Vue's inject function. Must be called inside setup() or an active injection context.

```APIDOC
## Function: `useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient`

### Description
Retrieves the `QueryClient` installed by `VueQueryPlugin`, via Vue's `inject`. Must be called inside `setup()` or another function that supports an injection context.

### Parameters
- **id** (`string`, optional, default: `''`) - The `queryClientKey` passed to `VueQueryPlugin` — only needed when multiple `QueryClient`s are installed in the same app.

### Returns
- **QueryClient** - The installed `QueryClient` instance.

### Throws
- Throws an error if called outside an injection context, or if no `QueryClient` was installed via `VueQueryPlugin`.

### Example
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```
```

### Basic TanStack Solid Query setup with useQuery and QueryClientProvider

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Wrap the application in a QueryClientProvider and pass a QueryClient instance. Inside components, use useQuery with an accessor function returning query options and handle loading, error, and success states using SolidJS control flow components.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Switch, Match, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const query = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={query.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.error}>
          <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isSuccess}>
          <For each={query.data}>{(todo) => <p>{todo.title}</p>}</For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### Execute useQuery in a Vue component with <script setup>

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/installation.md

Demonstrates invoking useQuery within a Vue Single-File Component using the <script setup> Composition API syntax.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const { isPending, isFetching, isError, data, error } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: getTodos,
})
</script>

<template>...</template>
```

--------------------------------

### Set up QueryClientProvider and fetch data with createQuery

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/overview.md

Configure QueryClientProvider at the project root and consume createQuery inside child components. Arguments to createQuery must be wrapped in a function to maintain reactivity in Svelte.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: () => fetchTodos(),
  }))
</script>

<div>
  {#if query.isPending}
    <p>Loading...</p>
  {:else if query.isError}
    <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
  {:else if query.isSuccess}
    {#each query.data as todo}
      <p>{todo.title}</p>
    {/each}
  {/if}
</div>
```

```bash

--------------------------------

### new QueriesObserver(client, queries, options?)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueriesObserver.md

Initializes a new QueriesObserver instance to monitor multiple queries at once.

```APIDOC
### Constructor

```ts
new QueriesObserver<TCombinedResult>(
   client: QueryClient, 
   queries: QueryObserverOptions<any, any, any, any, any, never>[], 
   options?: QueriesObserverOptions<TCombinedResult>
): QueriesObserver<TCombinedResult>;
```

### Parameters

- **client** (`QueryClient`) - The QueryClient instance.
- **queries** (`QueryObserverOptions<any, any, any, any, any, never>[]`) - An array of query observer configuration options.
- **options** (`QueriesObserverOptions<TCombinedResult>`, *optional*) - Additional options for the queries observer, such as a combine function.

### Returns

- `QueriesObserver<TCombinedResult>` - A new instance of QueriesObserver.

### Example

```ts
const observer = new QueriesObserver(queryClient, [
  { queryKey: ['post', 1], queryFn: fetchPost },
  { queryKey: ['post', 2], queryFn: fetchPost },
])

const unsubscribe = observer.subscribe((result) => {
  console.log(result)
})
```
```

--------------------------------

### Install @tanstack/vue-query using pnpm

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/vue-query/README.md

Install the Vue Query package using the pnpm package manager.

```bash
$ pnpm add @tanstack/vue-query
```

--------------------------------

### Install @tanstack/svelte-query-devtools using yarn

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/devtools.md

Installs the TanStack Svelte Query devtools package using yarn.

```bash
yarn add @tanstack/svelte-query-devtools
```
